chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: First hearing Louis Armstrong in person; promoter Jessie Johnson
summary: Dance dates Carroll Dickerson's band with Armstrong at about 1928. Thomas names the Chauffeurs' Club and promoter Jessie Johnson, who admired Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, Joe, when was it then that you first heard Louis Armstrong in person?
Louis Armstrong. Let me see. Had to be St. Louis.
Oh, as late as that? You didn't hear him come in with Frank Malinborn?
Oh, no. Had to be St. Louis. In fact, see Carroll Dickerson had a band out of Chicago.
I thought it was around '28. Thanks for getting me up to date. Man, you got a cigarette?
No, I haven't but I'll get some.

I don't want to lose the sequence. ... place in St. Louis called the Chauffer's Club. Thank you very much, because there was a tremendous guy there. I'm passing by a whole lot of things. Atremendous guy there by the name of
Jessie? That's no relation to, wait a minute, who am I thinking of?
You might be thinking of Mandy Johnson. Menzie

Well, now I'm getting a little ... (lot of) reliving your life and it's frightening some times but it's pleasurable. And, we talk about the people you've known and especially the great man and the great trumpet player like -- I always thought he was the greatest and I still think he is -- Louis Armstrong.
But, this Jessie Johnson that you talked about, Jessie Johnson was what, a band leader?

Promoter. We worked for Jessie Johnson ... in this business need now promotion. Jessie Johnson promoted music all over that area. At that time, there were fellows, had different areas promoted different things, you know, musical fellows. And, Jessie was crazy about Louis Armstrong personally. I mean his horn first but the man got added to it. Tremendous person. And I worked for him, I got off of work kind of early in those days. I got off of work around 1 o'clock.
